chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Dawud ibn Al-Husayn has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah be pleased with them both - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab, from Al-Hakam ibn Miskin, from Dawud ibn Al-Husayn Al-Asadi, who was a freed servant.

key_terms.دَاوُدَ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Dawud ibn Al-Husayn, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I narrated it / I transmitted it
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator in Shia hadith literature

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Dawud ibn Al-Husayn's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq explicitly links his narration of Dawud ibn Al-Husayn to his teacher, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, thereby anchoring the chain within the prominent Kufan scholarly tradition. By specifying Dawud as a *mawla* (freedman), the text highlights the social diversity of early hadith transmitters and reinforces the reliability of this specific lineage for verifying the authenticity of reports in *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*.
